what: Plain-English explainer for every sleeve, keyed by lane id. Read by the GrokBot Desk terminal.

glossary.Fear day: A day when QQQ (the Nasdaq-100 fund) trades below its prior close. Most sleeves only buy on fear days, and only if the stock is down too.
glossary.Cyan signal: The UT-Bot trend indicator flips to buy while the engine's trend votes agree.
glossary.Green signal: The 8-period average crosses above the 21-period average while the engine's trend votes agree.
glossary.Swing signal: Most of the engine's 7 trend and momentum votes turn bullish at once.
glossary.Signal engine: The desk's signal engine. It computes 7 trend and momentum votes per stock and the Cyan, Green and Swing signals.
glossary.Sleeve: One strategy with its own rules and budget. Each desk runs many sleeves side by side.
glossary.Tier A: A signal that passes every research veto and has at least two independent supporting signals.
glossary.Time exit: The position is sold after a fixed number of trading days, weeks or bars, whatever the price.

1h.name: 1H Swing
1h.summary: Hourly swing trades on a fixed watch list, bought only while QQQ and the stock are both down on the day.
1h.looks_for: On a closed hourly bar, a Swing buy signal (at least 5 of the engine's 7 trend and momentum votes are bullish and bulls beat bears by 4 or more, confirmed by an early 'monitor' buy on that bar or one of the 3 before it) from the signal engine. The stock must be on the desk's frozen hourly swing watch list or match an active researched hourly setup.
1h.entry: Within 30 minutes after the signal bar, it buys only while QQQ and the stock are both below their prior daily close (otherwise it keeps checking until the 30 minutes run out). It sends one limit order, good for that day only: the current price plus 1%, never above 3% over the signal-day close.
1h.exit: Follows the signal's research-calibrated exit plan. For watch-list names that plan is no stop loss and a time exit after 60 hourly bars (about 9 trading days). The hold is counted from the signal bar. Every sale is one limit sell order at the price minus 1%; a time exit is sent at the desk check about 20 minutes before its exit time.
1h.sizing: About $1,725 per stock, in whole shares, and never more than 1% of the stock's average daily dollar volume. Up to 30 positions at once, within a $51,750 sleeve budget. Every buy also needs free cash in the account.
1h.why: In research, these hourly signals averaged +0.47% per trade with 48% winners over 3,705 out-of-sample trades. The watch list was, so live results are the real test.
1h.source: the signal engine via the desk's signal tracker

1d.name: 1D Green

1d.entry: Waits for a fear day. On any of the 5 trading days after the signal, between 40 and 10 minutes before the close, it buys only if QQQ is below yesterday's close, the stock is at or below its own yesterday's close, and the price is no more than 2% above the signal-day close. It sends one limit order, good for that day only: the current price plus 1%, never above that 2% cap. No fear day in 5 days: the signal is skipped.
1d.exit: No stop loss. Some researched setups also take profit early: all out at +20%, or sell a third at +30% and trail the rest 2 ATR below the high, still within 40 days. The hold is counted from the fill. Every sale is one limit sell order at the price minus 1%; a time exit is sent at the desk check about 20 minutes before its exit time.
1d.sizing: About $1,725 per stock, in whole shares, and never more than 1% of the stock's average daily dollar volume. Up to 5 positions at once, within a $8,625 sleeve budget. Every buy also needs free cash in the account.
1d.why: In research these signals won 54% of the time and averaged +3.71% per trade over 849 trades. Buying only on red days for both the market and the stock avoids chasing a stock that has already jumped.
1d.source: the signal engine via the desk's signal tracker
